title: A 12-Year-Old Fixes Old Toys for Kids in Need
summary:
A soft toy can mean a lot to a child in a hard time. That is why Red Cross helpers keep stuffed animals ready for children hurt by disasters. But earlier this year, the Red Cross in North Carolina ran low. More home fires meant its supply was running short.

Red Cross worker Jon McCollum asked the community for help. His call caught the eye of 12-year-old Sadie Hutson. Sadie and her mother started buying old stuffed animals from thrift stores. Then Sadie fixed each toy. She washed it, sewed up torn seams, and even put in new stuffing.

By early summer, Sadie had fixed and given away 114 bears, rabbits, puppies and other stuffed toys. In September 2026, the Red Cross gave her a Young Humanitarian Award.

Sadie was happy to get the award, but that was not why she did it. 'Hearing the stories was a little heartbreaking,' she said. 'That's why I did it.' She hopes her story will inspire other young people to help, and she plans to keep fixing toys for children who need comfort.
why_it_matters: It shows that even a kid can make a real difference for other children by using simple skills to help.
